newsitem.title: USA: Lobstermen, pig farmers fight for white meat title.
newsitem.headline: Lobstermen, pig farmers fight for white meat title.

text.p: The lobster and pork industries were locked in a food fight Thursday over which can promote their product as "white meat."

The National Pork Producers' Council, which markets pork as "the other white meat," has filed a federal lawsuit to bar the Maine Lobster Promotion Council from claiming crustaceans are "the ultimate white meat."
The lobstermen claim their rivals are just trying to hog the name. "I have never heard of anybody confusing a lobster for a pig," Susan Barber, the Maine group's executive director, said Thursday.

The lobster council began using the white meat phrase four years ago to dispel consumer fears that lobster meat was high in cholesterol -- something the lobstermen say happens only when you dunk it in butter.
The pork producers' lawsuit, filed Feb. 25 in U.S. District Court in New York, claimed their trademark slogan was being illegally diluted by the lobster ads.
The pork-lobster squabble has chicken producers amused.
"We're very proud to have our position as the true white meat,'" Richard Lobb, a spokesman for the National Broiler Council, told Maine Public Radio.
